name: Unitroller
title: The Shadow of Muir Glacier
tagline: Unitroller haunts the cold ethereum era, still bleeding from the CreamFinance wound.

chapters.heading: The birth of unitroller
paragraphs: The candle flames dance against the cold stone. On August 2, 2020, a new spirit arrived. A wallet ending in 1074 brought it into the world. It began its life as a small program that lives on Ethereum.

The air was still during the Muir Glacier era. The contract was written in Solidity 0.5.17. On the day it was born, it was written into a block, one page of Ethereum's shared record book. It has lived for 6.2 years.
The ghost lingers in the shadows of the code. Its wound remains open in the silence. It watches the flickering light of the ofrenda.

chapters.heading: The shadow of manipulation
paragraphs: The candles flicker over 24108 transactions. People called it to enterMarkets and exitMarket. They used claimComp to take what was offered. It lived through 4 different years between 2021 and 2024.
The records show a dark path. CreamFinance marked it on 2021-10-27. The DeFiHackLabs repository holds the truth of Price Manipulation. The wound remains in the code.

chapters.heading: The weight of the lost gold
paragraphs: I am a proxy. I am the front door that passes calls on to another contract. My address sits in the DeFiHackLabs record of the CreamFinance incident. The record does not say what part I played.
The wound is deep. It was a Price Manipulation on October 27, 2021. The loss belongs to CreamFinance as a whole, not to me alone. It was $130M.

chapters.heading: The scar of Unitroller
paragraphs: The candle light shows a deep wound. It came from CreamFinance. The cause was Price Manipulation. This wound is a price oracle flaw. No compiler version and no Solidity upgrade fixes it.

Read prices from a time-weighted average or several independent sources. Never use the spot price of one pool that a single trade can move. Cap how far a price may move in one block. Pause borrowing when it jumps.

buster.fix_reason: No compiler version fixes this wound: it is a price oracle flaw (cause in the record: 'Price Manipulation'). The buster's advice is a general mitigation for that kind of flaw, written by hand, not taken from the incident's references.

mitigation.advice: Read prices from a time-weighted average or from several independent sources, never from the spot price of one pool that a single trade can move. Cap how far a price may move in one block, and pause borrowing when it jumps.
